u: The single biggest cause is a billing error in spring 2025. Between May 14 and June 7, 2025, our system credited merchants for extra carrier fees instead of charging them, about 15,000 times across 137 merchants. That one error accounts for about $116,000, roughly a fifth of all the money we have not collected. The billing team should confirm what happened, and we should decide whether to correct those merchant balances or write the loss off.

Before mid May 2025 we had no way to pass extra carrier fees on to merchants at all. USPS packaging fees from early 2025 were never collected, about $40,000 at Easy Clothes North America, Primo Golf Apparel, Wig Studio 1 and ENRFORCE alone. USPS has charged almost none of these fees since July 2025, so this is an old backlog rather than a growing problem.

Three problems are still costing us money every month and should be fixed first: import taxes on District Vision's international FedEx orders, Izzy Zero Waste Beauty being charged less than its label price, and oversized boxes at Pond Pro Canada. Together they cost about $4,400 in the last 30 days.
o: Freckled Poppy is the largest over-billed account. DHL eCommerce charges us slightly less than our label price on almost every Freckled Poppy order, about $17,000 so far and still growing. This is extra margin rather than an error, but the price may be set higher than intended.

Freckled Poppy, RESA and Girls Crew were charged about $38,000 more for extra carrier fees than the carriers finally billed us, between August 2025 and January 2026. These merchants are likely owed credits.

A small USPS postage fee on By Alexa Rae and Camp Snap labels adds about $1,100 a month across roughly 93,000 labels. This comes from how those accounts are priced, and should be confirmed as intended.

u|689a67d5f8907cd382f0497e|FedEx|C|prior.headline: FedEx import tax bills on international orders are only partly passed on
u|689a67d5f8907cd382f0497e|FedEx|C|prior.what: District Vision ships many orders overseas with FedEx. When those packages cross a border, the destination country charges import taxes such as customs duty and VAT. FedEx pays these taxes and bills us weeks later. Since October 2025, these late bills have left {amount} unpaid across {shipments} shipments.
u|689a67d5f8907cd382f0497e|FedEx|C|prior.why: We do pass some of these late tax bills on to District Vision, about $28,000 so far, but not all of them, so part of each bill stays with us. The labels also understate weight on most of these shipments, about 1 pound on the label versus 3.6 pounds measured by FedEx, which widens the gap. This is still happening, with {last30} in the last 30 days.
fix: Make sure every late import tax bill from FedEx is charged to District Vision automatically, not just some of them.
Bill District Vision for the {amount} still outstanding.
Ask District Vision to correct the package weights in their store, and consider shipping international orders with import taxes paid up front so the full cost is known at checkout.

u|656cb9c5293f8600072136f7|USPS|M|mercha.what: Between May 14 and June 7, 2025, USPS charged us extra fees on {shipments} Easy Clothes North America shipments. We paid the fee and also gave the merchant money back, losing {amount}.
u|656cb9c5293f8600072136f7|USPS|M|mercha.why: This was not specific to Easy Clothes. In the same three weeks, every extra fee charge to merchants went the wrong way: about 15,000 charges at 137 merchants, worth about $65,000, were posted as credits instead of charges. From mid June 2025 the charges went the right way again, and nothing new has happened at this merchant since.
fix: Confirm with the billing team that fee charges posted between May 14 and June 7, 2025 were credited by mistake.
Decide as a company whether to correct the affected merchant balances or write the loss off. At Easy Clothes, this error is worth {amount}.
Add a check that stops any fee charge to a merchant from posting as a credit.

u|69726ff1809a5cc0e538c8cd|UPS|C|currenc.headline: Pond Pro Canada's UPS bills are well above the label price, and still growing
u|69726ff1809a5cc0e538c8cd|UPS|C|currenc.what: Pond Pro Canada ships from Canada with UPS, and UPS bills those shipments in Canadian dollars. Since July 2026, the final bills, converted to US dollars, came in {amount} above our label price across {shipments} shipments. This is still happening, with {last30} in the last 30 days.
u|69726ff1809a5cc0e538c8cd|UPS|C|currenc.why: There are two causes. First, the boxes are much bigger than declared: the label says 8 by 8 by 6 inches, but UPS measured about 19 by 13 by 13 inches on every shipment it measured, and bigger boxes cost more to ship. Second, the final UPS bills include Canadian sales tax and fuel charges that our label price does not cover.
fix: Correct the box size saved for Pond Pro Canada's products so labels are priced on the real box.
Make sure Canadian sales tax and fuel charges from UPS are charged to the merchant.
Bill the {amount} difference.
